examples.en: The ball the batter hit became a grounder.
The shortstop caught the ground ball and threw it to first base.
The runner advanced to third on an infield grounder.
It was a pity that he grounded out.
That pitcher is good at inducing ground balls.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 땅볼보다 뜬공을 많이 쳐요.
examples.en: That player hits more fly balls than ground balls.

explain: 야구에서 땅 위로 구르는 공을 말해요. 반대로 공중으로 뜨는 공은 '뜬공'이라고 해요. '땅볼 아웃', '내야 땅볼'처럼 중계나 기사에서 자주 들어요.
explain_en: It is a baseball term for a ball that rolls along the ground. The opposite, a ball hit into the air, is a '뜬공'. You often hear it as '땅볼 아웃' or '내야 땅볼' in broadcasts and articles.

examples.en: This singer has a wide repertoire.
The pianist is preparing a new repertoire.
My father's repertoire of stories is always the same.
I added a Korean song to the repertoire too.
My cooking repertoire has grown a lot too.
Today's concert program is all classical.

explain: 공연에서는 연주나 노래할 수 있는 작품 목록을 말하고, 일상에서는 늘 하는 이야기나 농담을 비유할 때도 써요. 노래방에서 가장 자신 있는 노래는 '십팔번'이라고 해요. 표준 표기는 '레퍼토리'예요.
explain_en: On stage 레퍼토리 is the list of works a performer can play or sing, and in daily life it can describe someone's usual stories or jokes. The song you are best at in karaoke is called 십팔번. The standard spelling is 레퍼토리.

examples.en: In basketball you need to grab rebounds well.
That player gets a lot of rebounds.
Tall players have the advantage in rebounding.
After a diet ends, it is easy for weight to bounce back.
The flow of the game changed because of the rebound.
The number of rebounds decided the team's win or loss.

explain: 농구에서는 슛이 빗나가 튕긴 공을 잡는 걸 말하고, 다이어트 뒤에 살이 다시 찌는 것도 '리바운드'라고 해요. 영어 'rebound'를 그대로 쓰는 외래어라서 한국어 말로 바꿔 쓰는 일은 드물어요.
explain_en: In basketball it means grabbing the ball that bounces off a missed shot, and weight coming back after a diet is also called 리바운드. It is an English loanword used as is, and Korean replacements are rare.

examples.ko: 이 그림은 완성이 아니라 아직 밑그림이에요.
examples.en: This picture isn't finished; it's still just a rough sketch.
I drew the underdrawing first in pencil.
Try painting colors on top of the underdrawing.
You can feel the skill even from the underdrawing alone.

examples.ko: 이 계획은 아직 큰 밑그림일 뿐이에요.
examples.en: This plan is still just a big-picture outline.
The underdrawing was wrong, so I drew it again.

explain: 그림에서 색을 칠하기 전에 그리는 대략의 선 그림이에요. 계획이나 구상이 아직 대략적인 단계일 때 '밑그림을 그리다'라고 비유해서도 많이 말해요. 비슷한 말로 '스케치'도 쓰지만, 계획에는 밑그림이 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It is the rough line drawing made before applying color. It is also widely used figuratively, as in '밑그림을 그리다', when a plan is still at the rough stage. '스케치' is similar, but for plans '밑그림' sounds more natural.

examples.ko: 우리 팀이 한 점 차로 분패했어요.
examples.en: Our team lost by just one point.
It was a pity that we lost narrowly in the final.
Even if we lose narrowly, let's do our best to the end.
The fans comforted the player who lost so narrowly.
I'm worried we might lose a close one again.
I practiced hard so as not to lose narrowly this time.

explain: 그냥 '지다'보다 아깝고 분한 마음이 담겨 있어서, 점수 차가 작거나 거의 이길 뻔한 경기에 써요. 스포츠 뉴스에 자주 나와요. 반대로 이기는 쪽은 '승리하다', '이기다'라고 해요.
explain_en: Unlike plain '지다', it carries a feeling of regret and frustration, so it fits games lost by a small margin or almost won. It often appears in sports news. The opposite is '승리하다' or '이기다'.

en: current of thought; (literary or artistic) movement

examples.ko: 르네상스는 유럽 문화에 큰 영향을 준 사조예요.
examples.en: The Renaissance was a movement that greatly influenced European culture.

examples.ko: 미술 시간에 인상주의 같은 여러 사조를 배웠어요.
examples.en: In art class, I learned about various movements such as Impressionism.
As the times changed, literary trends changed too.

examples.ko: 새로운 사조는 기존 예술에 대한 반발에서 나오기도 해요.
examples.en: A new movement sometimes comes from a reaction against existing art.

examples.ko: 이 소설은 당시 유행하던 사조의 영향을 받았어요.
examples.en: This novel was influenced by the trend that was popular at the time.

examples.ko: 그 화가는 어떤 사조에도 속하지 않는 독특한 그림을 그렸어요.
examples.en: That painter made unique pictures that belong to no movement.

explain: '문예 사조', '사상 사조'처럼 문학, 미술, 사상 같은 분야의 큰 흐름을 말할 때 써요. 단순한 유행은 '유행'이나 '트렌드'라고 해요. 낭만주의, 인상주의처럼 '~주의'와 같이 나오는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: It refers to a major current in fields like literature, art and philosophy, as in '문예 사조' and '사상 사조'. A simple fad is called '유행' or '트렌드'. It often comes up together with '~주의' names such as Romanticism and Impressionism.

examples.en: Our team's defensive line is so shaky.
The defense wavered, and we conceded the first goal.

examples.ko: 새로 온 선수가 수비진에 큰 힘이 돼요.
examples.en: The newly arrived player is a big help to the defense.
The coach rearranged the defensive line.
The defenders and the goalkeeper work well together.
The defense also stayed focused throughout the match.

explain: '수비수'는 선수 한 명이고, '수비진'은 수비를 맡은 선수들 전체를 말해요. 공격을 맡은 쪽은 '공격진'이라고 해요.
explain_en: A '수비수' is a single defender, while '수비진' is the whole group of players in charge of defense. The attacking group is called '공격진'.

examples.en: I think this movie is really a quality work.

examples.ko: 올해 나온 소설 중에서 수준작을 골랐어요.
examples.en: I picked out a quality piece from the novels released this year.
The exhibition had many fine works, so it was worth seeing.
Critics picked this drama as a quality work.

examples.ko: 수준작인데도 사람들이 잘 모르는 것 같아요.
examples.en: It's a fine work, yet it seems people don't know it well.

examples.ko: 첫 작품이 수준작이라서 다음 작품이 기대돼요.
examples.en: Since the first work was so good, I'm looking forward to the next.

explain: 영화, 소설, 드라마, 전시 같은 작품이 꽤 잘 만들어졌다고 칭찬할 때 써요. 보통 '걸작'이나 '명작'보다 가볍고 편하게 쓰는 말이에요. '수준작으로 꼽히다', '수준작이라고 평가하다'처럼 자주 써요.
explain_en: Used to praise a work such as a film, novel, drama or exhibit as well made. It is usually lighter and more casual than '걸작' (masterpiece) or '명작' (classic). Common uses are '수준작으로 꼽히다' (be counted as a quality work) and '수준작이라고 평가하다' (evaluate as a quality work).

examples.en: Our team earned three league points.
You get three points for a win and one for a draw.

examples.ko: 승점이 같으면 골 득실로 순위를 정해요.
examples.en: If the points are tied, rank is decided by goal difference.
The gap in points narrowed in the last match.
We are ahead by one point.

examples.ko: 승점을 많이 쌓아서 올해는 순위가 많이 올랐어요.
examples.en: We piled up many points, so our ranking rose a lot this year.

explain: 축구 같은 리그 경기에서 이기면 3점, 비기면 1점을 주는 점수예요. 한 경기에서 넣은 점수는 '득점', 리그 순위를 정하는 점수는 '승점'이라서 둘이 달라요. 스포츠 뉴스와 중계에서 자주 들려요.
explain_en: In league sports like soccer, a win gives 3 and a draw 1. Goals scored in one match are '득점', while '승점' is what decides the league standings, so the two differ. You hear it often in sports news and broadcasts.

examples.en: They say that movie was a box-office flop.
My first cake was a complete failure.
This dish was a flop, so I have to throw it away.
Even a failed work is a valuable experience.
That game was rated as a failure.

examples.ko: 제 첫 그림은 실패작이지만 버리지 않았어요.
examples.en: My first painting was a failure, but I didn't throw it away.

explain: 만든 결과물에 쓰는 말로, 요리, 영화, 그림, 제품 모두 가능해요. 반대말은 '성공작'이고, 아주 훌륭한 작품은 '걸작'이라고 해요. 사람에게는 쓰지 않고 '실패자'를 따로 써요.
explain_en: It is used for things people made, such as dishes, films, paintings and products. The opposite is '성공작', and an outstanding work is a '걸작'. It is not used for people; '실패자' is a separate word.

examples.ko: 그 영화는 유명한 작품의 아류라는 평을 받았어요.
examples.en: That movie was criticized as a knockoff of a famous work.

examples.ko: 아류 소리를 듣지 않으려면 나만의 색이 필요해요.
examples.en: To avoid being called a copycat, you need your own style.

examples.ko: 이 가수는 선배 가수의 아류로 보이기 싫어해요.
examples.en: This singer doesn't want to be seen as an imitation of a senior singer.

examples.ko: 유행하던 게임의 아류가 너무 많이 나왔어요.
examples.en: Far too many knockoffs of the trendy game came out.
The director was upset by criticism that the film was derivative.

examples.ko: 처음엔 아류였지만 지금은 독자적인 스타일을 만들었어요.
examples.en: He started out as an imitator, but now he has made his own style.

explain: 독창성 없이 다른 유명한 것을 따라 한 사람이나 작품을 낮춰 말할 때 써요. 작품에는 '아류작'이라고도 하고, 칭찬으로는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: It is used to disparage a person or work that follows a famous original without being original. For works you can also say '아류작', and it is never a compliment.

examples.ko: 그 평론가는 신간 소설을 심하게 악평했어요.
examples.en: That critic harshly panned the new novel.

examples.ko: 영화가 개봉하자마자 악평이 쏟아졌지만 관객 수는 꾸준히 늘었어요.
examples.en: Harsh reviews poured in as soon as the film opened, but attendance kept growing.

examples.ko: 새로 연 식당은 서비스에 대한 악평 때문에 한동안 손님이 줄었어요.
examples.en: The newly opened restaurant lost customers for a while because of bad reviews about its service.

examples.ko: 기자가 신제품을 악평하는 바람에 회사가 곤란해졌어요.
examples.en: The company was put in a difficult position because a reporter slammed the new product.

examples.ko: 직접 먹어 보지도 않고 악평하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't badmouth it without even trying it yourself.

examples.ko: 사람들이 그 소설을 악평해도 저는 재미있게 읽었어요.
examples.en: Even though people panned the novel, I enjoyed reading it.

explain: 작품, 제품, 가게 등을 나쁘게 평가할 때 써요. '혹평하다'와 비슷하고 반의어는 '호평하다'예요. 명사 '악평'은 '악평을 받다', '악평이 쏟아지다'처럼 자주 말해요.
explain_en: Use it when you evaluate a work, product or shop negatively. It is close to '혹평하다', and its antonym is '호평하다'. The noun '악평' is common in phrases like '악평을 받다' and '악평이 쏟아지다'.

examples.ko: 우리 팀은 지금 오 연승 중이에요.
examples.en: Our team is on a five-game winning streak right now.

examples.ko: 그 선수의 연승 기록이 드디어 끝났어요.
examples.en: That player's winning streak has finally ended.
We practice every day to keep the winning streak going.

examples.ko: 열 경기 연승은 쉬운 일이 아니에요.
examples.en: Winning ten games in a row is not easy.
Thanks to the winning streak, the team became more popular.

examples.ko: 감독은 연승보다 선수들의 건강이 더 중요하다고 했어요.
examples.en: The coach said the players' health matters more than a winning streak.

explain: 숫자 뒤에 붙여 '삼 연승', '십 연승'처럼 말해요. 반대말은 '연패'예요. '연승을 달리다', '연승을 이어 가다'처럼 스포츠 뉴스에서 자주 들려요.
explain_en: Attach a number to it, as in '삼 연승' or '십 연승'. The opposite is '연패' (a losing streak). Sports news often says '연승을 달리다' or '연승을 이어 가다'.

en: successive victories; a series of wins

examples.ko: 우리 팀이 올해 연전연승을 이어 가고 있어요.
examples.en: Our team is keeping up a winning streak this year.
That player won the tournament with win after win.
A reporter asked what the secret to the winning streak was.
The winning streak has finally come to an end.
At first it was win after win, but we lost the last game.
Don't just hope for win after win; enjoy it while you play.

explain: 짝이 되는 말은 '연전연패'예요. 스포츠 뉴스나 게임 이야기에서 많이 나와요. '연승'만 써도 통하지만 연전연승은 싸울 때마다 이긴다는 느낌이 더 강해요.
explain_en: Its opposite is '연전연패' (a string of losses). It shows up often in sports news and talk about games. '연승' alone also works, but 연전연승 feels stronger, as if the team wins every time it plays.

examples.en: The referee pulled out a yellow card for that player.
He committed a foul and got a yellow card.
Two yellow cards means you're sent off.

examples.ko: 우리 팀 수비수는 벌써 옐로카드 한 장을 받았어요.
examples.en: Our team's defender has already received one yellow card.

examples.ko: 옐로카드 때문에 다음 경기에 못 나온대요.
examples.en: I heard he can't play in the next match because of his yellow cards.

examples.ko: 오늘 경기는 옐로카드가 너무 많이 나왔어요.
examples.en: Too many yellow cards were shown in today's match.

explain: 축구에서 심판이 경고를 줄 때 보여 주는 카드예요. 한 경기에서 두 장을 받으면 '레드카드'로 퇴장당해요. 일상에서 '옐로카드를 받았다'고 하면 가벼운 경고를 받았다는 농담으로도 써요.
explain_en: It is the card a referee shows to give a warning in soccer. Two in one match leads to a '레드카드' and being sent off. In daily life, '옐로카드를 받았다' can also jokingly mean you got a mild warning.

examples.en: The child pushed the tumbler doll and laughed out loud.
A tumbler doll stands right back up even if you knock it over.

examples.ko: 책상 위에 빨간 오뚝이 인형이 놓여 있어요.
examples.en: A red tumbler doll sits on the desk.
Grandfather bought a tumbler doll for his grandchild.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 오뚝이처럼 다시 일어나 우승했어요.
examples.en: That athlete bounced back like a tumbler doll and won.

examples.ko: 오뚝이 정신으로 다시 한번 도전해 볼게요.
examples.en: I'll try once more with a never-give-up spirit.

explain: 밑이 둥글고 무거워서 넘어뜨려도 다시 서는 전통 장난감이에요. 실패해도 포기하지 않고 다시 일어나는 사람을 비유할 때 자주 써요. 이때는 '오뚝이처럼 일어서다'로 말해요.

phrases.en: Even after his business failed, he bounced back.
phrases.nuance_ko: 넘어져도 포기하지 않고 다시 일어서는 끈기를 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to praise someone's resilience in getting back up after falling.

explain_en: It is a traditional toy with a round, weighted bottom that rights itself after being knocked over. It is often used as a metaphor for a person who gets back up after failure. In that sense you say '오뚝이처럼 일어서다'.

examples.ko: 아이들이 공원에서 요요를 가지고 놀고 있어요.
examples.en: Children are playing with a yo-yo in the park.

examples.ko: 요요는 줄을 잘 감는 것이 중요해요.
examples.en: With a yo-yo, winding the string well is important.

examples.ko: 저는 어렸을 때 요요 대회에 나간 적이 있어요.
examples.en: When I was young I entered a yo-yo contest.
The yo-yo moves up and down quickly.
I got a sparkly yo-yo as a birthday present.

examples.ko: 다이어트가 끝나자마자 요요 현상이 와서 다시 살이 쪘어요.
examples.en: As soon as my diet ended, the yo-yo effect came and I gained weight again.

explain: 장난감 이름이지만 다이어트 뒤에 살이 다시 찌는 것도 '요요 현상'이라고 불러요. 줄을 감았다 풀며 오르내리는 모습에서 나온 비유예요. 두 번째 쓰임은 일상 대화에서도 정말 많이 들어요.

phrases.example: 굶어서 뺐더니 요요 현상이 와서 더 쪘어요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다이어트 뒤에 뺀 살이 다시 찌는 것을 말해요. 줄여서 '요요가 오다'라고도 많이 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Weight coming back after a diet. People also shorten it to 요요가 오다.

explain_en: It is a toy, but weight returning after a diet is also called 요요 현상. The figure comes from the toy rising and falling on its string. The second use is very common in everyday Korean.

examples.en: I played throwing a flying disc with my dog in the park.
That athlete is a discus throw gold medalist.
The flying disc rode the wind and flew far.
On the weekend I played flying disc with friends.
The puppy ran back with the disc in its mouth.

examples.ko: 체육 시간에 원반 던지는 방법을 배웠어요.
examples.en: In PE class we learned how to throw a discus.

explain: 납작하고 둥근 물건을 말해요. 놀이용 '프리스비'를 가리킬 때가 많고, 육상 경기의 '원반던지기'에서도 써요. 컴퓨터의 '디스크'는 보통 외래어 그대로 말해요.
explain_en: It means a flat round object. It often refers to a frisbee for play, and it is also used in the track event 원반던지기. For a computer disk, Koreans usually just use the loanword 디스크.

examples.en: Experts judged that painting to be a forgery.
There was a big controversy over a forgery at the art museum.

examples.ko: 위작을 진짜처럼 속여 판 사람이 잡혔어요.
examples.en: The person who sold a forgery as if it were real was caught.
This piece of pottery is quite likely a fake.
It is really hard to tell a forgery from the genuine article.
A forgery of a famous painter's work showed up on the market.

explain: '가짜'보다 딱딱한 말이고, 그림·글씨·도자기 같은 예술품에 주로 써요. 반대말은 '진품'이고, 일상에서 물건이 가짜라고 할 때는 그냥 '가짜'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is more formal than '가짜' (fake) and is mainly used for artworks such as paintings, calligraphy and pottery. The opposite is '진품' (genuine article), and for everyday fake goods people just say '가짜'.

examples.en: I won the silver prize at the contest.
My younger sister won the silver prize at the drawing contest.
I got a culture gift certificate as the silver prize reward.

examples.ko: 아쉽게 금상은 못 탔지만 은상도 기뻐요.
examples.en: I missed the gold prize, but I'm happy with silver too.

examples.ko: 우리 팀이 은상에 뽑혀서 박수를 받았어요.
examples.en: Our team was chosen for the silver prize and got applause.
This year's silver prize went to a new writer.

explain: 시상할 때는 '금상 → 은상 → 동상' 순서로 말해요. 올림픽 같은 스포츠에서는 '금메달/은메달'이라고 하고, 대회나 공모전의 상에는 '금상/은상'을 써요. '은상을 받다/타다'로 말해요.
explain_en: Prizes are named in the order '금상 → 은상 → 동상'. In sports like the Olympics, people say '금메달/은메달', while '금상/은상' is used for contest and competition awards. You say '은상을 받다/타다'.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 이번 시즌에 타점을 100개나 올렸어요.
examples.en: That player drove in 100 runs this season.
A game-winning RBI came in yesterday's game.

examples.ko: 타점 순위 1위 선수가 우리 팀으로 왔어요.
examples.en: The player ranked first in RBIs joined our team.

examples.ko: 타점이 많은 타자는 팀에 큰 도움이 돼요.
examples.en: A batter with many RBIs is a big help to the team.

examples.ko: 중요한 순간에 타점을 올리는 선수를 좋아해요.
examples.en: I like players who drive in runs at key moments.

examples.ko: 올해 타점 기록은 작년보다 두 배 늘었어요.
examples.en: This year's RBI record has doubled compared to last year.

explain: '타점을 올리다', '타점을 내다'처럼 점수를 쌓는다는 느낌으로 동사와 같이 써요. '안타'는 공을 친 결과이고 '타점'은 그 덕분에 들어온 점수예요. 숫자를 앞에 붙여 '2타점 적시타'라고도 해요.
explain_en: 타점 goes with verbs like 타점을 올리다 and 타점을 내다, in the sense of piling up points. 안타 is the result of hitting the ball, while 타점 is the run that scores because of it. A number can go in front, as in 2타점 적시타.

examples.en: Critics gave this movie favorable reviews.
Many people praise the new app.

examples.ko: 그 식당을 호평하는 글이 인터넷에 많아요.
examples.en: There are many posts online praising that restaurant.
I read an article that praised the book and bought it.
My teacher spoke highly of my presentation.
The customers praised the taste of the food and left.

explain: 평가하는 사람이 주어일 때 '호평하다'를 써요. 평가를 받는 쪽에서는 '호평을 받다'라고 해요. 반대말은 '혹평하다'예요.
explain_en: Use '호평하다' when the person giving the review is the subject. From the side being reviewed, say '호평을 받다'. The opposite is '혹평하다'.
